# AIWinOps chapter sources

Retrieved 2026-10-19 from the [official AIWinOps product page](https://www.aiwin.com.tw/products/aiwinops). Images are stored locally as received. The chapter preserves the complete screenshot aspect ratio and adds large HTML captions for stage projection. Copyright remains with AIWin and the respective owners; no open-source license is implied.

The official `04-train.webp` asset visibly shows a dataset/project list and remains as a legacy asset. The revised chapter uses `prepare.webp` for data management, `annotate.webp` for AI-assisted polygon labeling and `training.webp` for training/validation analysis. Graph values remain the official demonstration values, not performance claims.

Product content covers project/data organization, labeling, classification, detection, segmentation, anomaly detection, model training, validation and deployment. No new accuracy, labor-saving or deployment-speed claims are added. Values appearing inside official screenshots are demonstration data.

The five case films and thumbnails remain the existing user-supplied Pitch v5 assets; see [vision credits](../vision/CREDITS.md). Diagrams and hardware illustrations are original SVG/CSS concepts, not equipment specifications, a live model run or measured customer outcomes. Model feedback does not imply unattended automatic retraining.

The WinEdge product/service/partner narrative is based on the user's stated strategy. Partner categories are an invitation to collaborate, not a list of signed agreements, commercial terms or endorsements.

## User-provided evidence used in the four-task scene

These existing assets were extracted from the user's AIWin Pitch v5; they are not new customers or newly produced results.

- `../pitch-wafer-map.png`: Wafer Map classification validation (Pitch p. 28).
- `../vision/caps.jpg`: bottle-cap defect annotation (Pitch p. 46, see vision credits).
- `../pitch-tooth-segmentation.png`: tooth-region segmentation technology demonstration; no diagnostic claim.
- `../pitch-mesh-anomaly.png`: normal mesh training/test samples; no defect annotation or accuracy claim is added.

Official manufacturing context was also checked at https://www.aiwin.com.tw/cases/manufacturing (holes, nuts and bottle-cap inspection), but the page's illustrative collage is not presented as a customer-site photograph. The revised keynote prioritizes the user's existing case footage and screenshots.

## AVS-553 product reveal

Retrieved 2026-10-19 from APLEX's official [AVS-553 announcement](https://www.aplex.com/index.php/content/news_detail/140?lang=1) and [product page](https://www.aplex.com/index.php/product/list/machine_vision_system/avs_-_5_series/3609/ACS-553). The legacy product URL contains ACS-553, but the displayed product is AVS-553.

Visual references:

- https://www.aplex.com/images/1758779573.png
- https://www.aplex.com/images/1758779683.png
- https://www.aplex.com/images/1758779753.png

`dist/avs553.js` is an original, code-native Three.js visual reconstruction of the chassis, cooling fins, I/O face, expansion covers and dual CRPS modules. No vendor photo or texture is embedded in the shipped model. The unit is rotated horizontally for the keynote's software-over-hardware composition. This is an appearance illustration, not installation guidance, a supported system configuration, a benchmark, or an endorsement of an AIWinOps bundle by APLEX. Moving fan blades, status LEDs, and light traces communicate operation conceptually.
